body:
## Summary

The four `active_weighted_ℑxy**` functions in
`src/Operators/interpolation_operators.jl` compute a masked average
over the 2x2 neighbor nodes around a point: a denominator counting how
many neighbors are not peripheral (wall/land), and a numerator meant to
sum only those same active neighbors.

The denominator correctly excluded peripheral nodes via
`not_peripheral_node`, but the numerator interpolated the raw field
unconditionally, with no masking. Any real (non-zero) value sitting at
a peripheral node — e.g. a velocity component stored at a closed wall
face — leaked into the numerator while still being correctly excluded
from the denominator's count, inflating the result near any boundary.

This is live code: e.g. `src/Forcings/relaxation.jl` uses
`active_weighted_ℑxyᶠᶜᶜ`/`active_weighted_ℑxyᶜᶠᶜ` for masked velocity
relaxation forcing near boundaries.

This PR zeroes the numerator's operand at peripheral nodes
(`active_masked_operand`), so the numerator and denominator agree on
which nodes count.

## Test plan

- Added `test_active_weighted_interpolation_masks_peripheral_nodes` to
  `test/unit/operators.jl`, covering `active_weighted_ℑxyᶜᶜᶜ` (interior
  cell + the active cell adjacent to a closed wall) and
  `active_weighted_ℑxyᶠᶠᶜ` (the peripheral wall node itself).
- Verified the new test fails against the pre-fix code (evaluates to
  1000.0 instead of 1.0, reproducing the leak) and passes with the fix.
- Full `test/unit/operators.jl` suite: 308 passed, 0 failed (up from
  305 pre-existing + 3 new).

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)
title: Fix peripheral-node leak in active_weighted_ℑxy** interpolation

body:
Closes #6532. Alternative to #6533.

With `WENOVectorInvariant`, the vertical advection term is `V⁻¹ (Φᵟ + δz(W̃ u))`, where the divergence flux `Φᵟ = û (cross + self divergence)` and the vertical flux are meant to cancel through continuity. The self divergence `δx(Ax u)` is WENO-upwinded while `W̃` interpolates `Az w` symmetrically, so the cancellation fails by `û (upwind − symmetric)(δx(Ax u))`. For a smooth velocity this residual is small, but where the face area jumps (partial cells with varying depth in the bottom level, latitude changes of `Ay`, curvilinear metrics) `δx(Ax u)` is dominated by the area change and the residual becomes a spurious momentum source. This is the jet reported in #6532.

This PR splits the transport divergence exactly with the product rule,

```
δx(Ax u) = ℑx(Ax) δx(u) + ℑx(u) δx(Ax)
```

and upwinds only the velocity difference `ℑx(Ax) δx(u)`, which is the self-advection term. The geometric part `ℑx(u) δx(Ax)` is interpolated symmetrically together with the cross divergence and the moving-grid term `Az Δr ∂t σ`, as the vertical transport `W̃` is. A uniform velocity then has zero vertical advection on any grid. The same split is applied to `VectorInvariantCrossVerticalUpwinding`.

The formulation stays vector invariant everywhere: there is no switch to flux form near the bottom.

### Results

Plateau channel from #6532 (10 days, ratio of partial-cell to whole-cell mixing):

| | mixing ratio | max \|u\| (m s⁻¹) |
|---|---|---|
| main | 2.50 | 0.212 |
| #6533 | 1.20 | 0.170 |
| flux form | 1.30 | 0.174 |
| this PR | 1.30 | 0.164 |

- Whole cells: identical to main up to round-off (4 × 10⁻⁸ relative).
- Cost: no measurable difference (128 × 64 × 24 `LatitudeLongitudeGrid` with `PartialCellBottom`, main 0.0212–0.0215 s per step, this PR 0.0209–0.0216 s per step on CPU over two runs each).

### Tests

New testset in `test/unit/vector_invariant_vertical_flux.jl`: the vertical advection of a uniform `u` and `v` vanishes on a `PartialCellBottom` grid with random bottom depths and on a `LatitudeLongitudeGrid`, for `WENOVectorInvariant()` and `WENOVectorInvariant(order=5)`. On main the residual is about 1.4 × 10⁻³ (partial cells) and 10⁻¹⁰ (sphere); with this PR it is at round-off.

Results change wherever face areas vary along the derivative direction (partial and shaved cells, the `v` equation on latitude-longitude grids, tripolar and cubed-sphere grids). No regression test uses `WENOVectorInvariant`.

body:
This is needed for PR #938 in `NumericalEarth`.

**Summary.** When a regional ocean model is driven at its open edges by data from a larger model or a reanalysis, water can slowly pile up in or drain out of the region, even though the outer model's sea level doesn't change that way. This PR adds an option that controls the total amount of water entering the region, while the boundary condition still decides where along the edges it comes in and goes out. It is the same approach that the NEMO and ROMS ocean models use, and it is off unless you ask for it.


`GravityWaveRadiationBoundaryCondition(...; target_transport = NetInflow(T; depth_exponent = p))`

Sides that share one `NetInflow` have their net inflow (∑ ∮U·n̂ dl, positive into the domain) pinned to `T` after the Flather fill of every barotropic substep, by one correction common to those sides. Each side keeps the shape of its Flather profile, and the split between the sides is left to Flather, as in NEMO (`bdy_vol`) and ROMS (`obc_volcons`). `T` is a number or a `Ref`, read at every barotropic step, so a callback can follow a volume target during a run.

The shift of each column's transport is proportional to `H^p`: `0` uniform per unit length, `1` a uniform velocity (NEMO, ROMS), `1/2` a uniform shift of the exterior free surface, which leaves a basin at rest for a common datum offset in the exterior η.

Motivation: regional ocean models nested in a reanalysis (NumericalEarth.jl#938). The exterior transport built from the parent drifts the child's volume by several Sv; pinning the net inflow to the parent's volume change removes it.

Tests (`test/test_open_boundary_conditions_hydrostatic.jl` or wherever the file lives):
- two sides sharing `NetInflow(0)` let no net water in; `NetInflow(Q/2)` lets in exactly Q/2 and the mean η rises by
  Q/2 Δt / A per step; a target in a `Ref` changed mid-run is followed.
- with a common exterior datum δ, `depth_exponent = 1/2` keeps a sloping basin at rest; `0` does not.

Limitation: the reduction is over one rank's faces; distributed grids are not supported yet.
title: NetInflow: pin the net inflow through GravityWaveRadiation sides, as NEMO and ROMS do

body:
## What was slow

On an `ImmersedBoundaryGrid`, `dot!` / `local_dot!` and `norm` were several times slower than the arithmetic they do. In a 360×160×20 immersed `LatitudeLongitudeGrid` hydrostatic model with the PCG `ImplicitFreeSurface`, the two `dot!`s and the `norm` per CG iteration were a large share of the time step. There were three causes:

1. `local_dot!` conditioned `a` and `b` separately and multiplied the two `ConditionalOperation`s, so the immersed condition (`immersed_peripheral_node | inactive_node`) was evaluated twice per point.
2. The product was a `BinaryOperation`. `interpolation_operator` picks its identity interpolators from a global counter (`identity1` … `identity6`), so the operation's type cannot be inferred. Each call allocated (~18–33 kB), dispatched dynamically, and cycled through six types that each had to be compiled.
3. `norm` (and `dot`) masked with the `Int` `0`, so the `ifelse` in `ConditionalOperation`'s `getindex` returned a `Union{Float64, Int}` inside the reduction loop.

## The change

- `local_dot!` reduces `dot_operand(a, b, condition)`. By default this is the same `condition_operand(a, …) * condition_operand(b, …)` as before.
- `AbstractOperations` adds a method for two `Field`s at the same location on the same grid. It builds the product as a `KernelFunctionOperation` (type-stable, no interpolation) and conditions that product once, with a mask of the field's element type. Because both masks hold at the same points, `ifelse(c, a * b, 0) == ifelse(c, a, 0) * ifelse(c, b, 0)`. Immersed, tripolar and reduced-field conditions come from the usual `condition_operand` dispatch on the operand's grid.
- The user `condition` keeps its meaning:
  - A condition function is still called with each conditioned operand (`OperandPairCondition`), so a condition that inspects `co.operand` behaves as before.
  - Array conditions and `nothing` do not depend on the operand, so they are evaluated once.
- Fields at different locations, and other `AbstractField`s, keep the previous path.
- `norm` masks with `zero(eltype(a))`.

The reduction is still the existing `Base.mapreducedim!` into a one-element array. On the GPU, GPUArrays handles it, so the code is architecture-generic and the distributed `dot!` (`local_dot!` followed by an all-reduce) is unchanged. Results differ only in summation order. The largest relative difference I observed was 1e-14, because the type-stable loop now vectorizes.

## Benchmarks

Previous vs. new implementation, A/B in the same process on a `LatitudeLongitudeGrid` (`Float64`). The immersed grid uses `GridFittedBottom` with about a third of the surface as land. The surface field is `ZFaceField(grid, indices=(:, :, Nz+1))`, as in the PCG free surface solver. The condition is `(i, j, k, grid, co) -> i > 3`. Times are minima from BenchmarkTools. Allocations are host bytes per call.

**Whole model:** 360×160×20 immersed lat-lon `HydrostaticFreeSurfaceModel` with the `:PreconditionedConjugateGradient` implicit free surface, `VectorInvariant` momentum advection and T/S tracers, on 1 CPU thread. The mean `time_step!` time went from **229.6 ms to 181.8 ms** (−21%).

`dot!, condition` on non-immersed grids allocates somewhat more than before (the `OperandPairCondition` carries two conditioned operands), and its time is unchanged.

## Tests

`test/unit/field.jl` gets a new testset, "Dot products and norms on (immersed, windowed) fields". It compares `dot!`, `dot` and `norm` with an explicit sum over the window's wet points (not in the immersed periphery and not inactive) and covers:
- non-immersed and immersed (`GridFittedBottom` with land, shallow and deep columns) `LatitudeLongitudeGrid`s, in `Float32` and `Float64`
- the surface-windowed `ZFaceField`, a full `CenterField` and a full `ZFaceField`, with random values in the immersed cells and halos
- no condition, an index condition, a condition on the operand's values, and a Boolean array condition (full fields only; see below)

I ran the new testset, `abstract_operations/conditional_reductions`, `general_solvers/preconditioned_conjugate_gradient`, `hydrostatic_free_surface/implicit_solver`, `poisson_solvers/conjugate_gradient` and `tripolar_grid/tripolar_grid` locally on CPU and CUDA, and all passed. The distributed `dot!` path was not run.

Not addressed here: a Boolean array `condition` on a windowed field is validated against the window's size, but `evaluate_condition` indexes it with the field's absolute indices, for example `k = Nz+1` into a size-1 dimension under `@inbounds`. This is true before and after this PR, so the new test uses array conditions only on full fields.
